results.summary: This design implements basic logic gates (AND, NOT, OR) and a clock divider on a Tiny Tapeout tile. The gates are wired to specific inputs: NOT to input a, AND to inputs b and c, and OR to inputs b and c. Testing involves setting the three inputs and verifying the outputs against a provided truth table. No external hardware is required, and the design serves as a simple educational example.

This circuit drives a seven-segment display to show the characters 'R.' when the input combination 10101010 is applied. It uses a combination of XOR and NOT gates to decode the input into the appropriate segment signals. The design is intended for educational purposes and requires no external hardware beyond the display itself. Testing is straightforward: apply the specified input and observe the output.

This design implements phase detectors (PFD and PD) and a frequency divider chain for PLL applications. It uses D flip-flops and AND gates for reset logic, with inputs for phase/frequency comparison and clock division. Testing involves applying square wave signals or manually toggling switches to observe lead/lag behavior. External hardware may include a signal generator or comparator.

Testing involves turning on one switch at a time and verifying the displayed number. No external hardware is required.
